acceptance: `evolve release-promote v1.2.3` with a fake gh (green run, assets present) clears prerelease (red: unknown command)
Missing assets or a red workflow refuses with exit 1 and leaves the release demoted
--rerun reruns the failed run before checking
fix: Add `evolve release-promote <tag> [--rerun]`, following the release-verify-* naming. With --rerun it reruns the tag's failed release workflow and waits for it. It then requires the release workflow green and `release-verify-binaries <tag>` passing before it clears prerelease. Exit 0 promoted; exit 1 refused, naming the red workflow or the missing assets; exit 2 on gh I/O. Document it in runtime-reference.md's demote-on-failure note.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: When a tag's release workflow fails, the demote-on-failure job marks the release prerelease=true so releases/latest keeps serving binaries (runtime-reference.md:317-327). After the fix, the operator re-promotes it with `gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/<id> -F prerelease=false` (:327) or reruns the workflow with `gh run rerun <release-run-id>` (skills/publish/SKILL.md:62). Nothing checks that the assets are present before the release becomes Latest again.
title: Re-promoting an auto-demoted release, or rerunning its failed release workflow, is raw `gh api` and `gh run rerun`; add `evolve release-promote`
